claim: Storing every executed episode (add-all) can be worse than a small fixed memory; measured drops of 3.7 to 12.1 points on all four agents (RegAgent 67.53 to 55.48, EHRAgent 16.75 to 13.05, AgentDriver 40.11 to 32.32, CIC-IoT 71.50 to 59.90).
agent_test: Run our agent on a task stream at equal tokens with add-all vs fixed seed bank vs gated add; compare final success.

claim: A quality gate on writes beats add-all, and gate quality matters: oracle (strict) filter > fine-tuned judge (C3, 300 labelled trajectories) > coarse prompted judges. Noisy gates can fall below fixed memory.
agent_test: Compare write gates: none, self-judge, verifier/test-based, oracle; same stream, equal tokens.

claim: Success-only retention is a common default (CASCADE, AWM, ExpeL recall store, Voyager) and gives large gains over zero-shot, but retention itself was never ablated in CASCADE; most of the gain is from having any case bank (48.33 to 63.76) and a learned retriever adds about 3 points (to 66.68).
agent_test: Ablate retention: success-only vs success+failure vs none, with retrieval fixed.

claim: Failures help only when the memory format can use them (distilled strategies or insights); raw failed episodes in success-oriented memories are flat or harmful (Synapse 40.6 to 41.7, AWM 44.4 to 42.2, ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7).
agent_test: Store failures as one-line lessons vs raw traces vs not at all; equal tokens.

claim: Retention rules that record only novel or uncovered cases (coverage-based) reach full coverage with far fewer cases than random: Towers of Hanoi 58 greedy cases cover all 6561 problems; 20 cases 90%.
agent_test: Test a novelty gate (add only if nearest stored case misses) vs add-success at equal bank size.

claim: Competence-aware deletion beats utility-based or random deletion when memory is capped: competence 100% (footprint) vs 80% (utility) vs 86% (random); at limit ~25, about 90% vs about 60%.
agent_test: Cap bank size; delete by coverage role (pivotal first kept) vs utility vs random. Note Pan 2005 says noisy data break the pivotal rule.

claim: History-based (utility after later retrieval) deletion works only with a reliable utility judge; periodic deletion cuts memory about 65-70% with small loss. A capped memory converges as the cap rises. Added: later-use utility deletion also works with embedding retrieval (ReMe +3.3 Pass@4 on BFCL-V3; MemRL Q vs success r 0.861; Sarukkai Q-based curation about +1 to +8 points).
agent_test: Cap at 100 vs 1000 records; delete by later-use utility vs age.

claim: Agents copy the output of the most similar stored case (experience-following), so a wrong stored case propagates to later tasks and compounds.
agent_test: Seed one wrong case and measure how often it is copied on near neighbours.

claim: Rewriting stored episodes into abstract lessons (consolidation) degrades memory over a stream and a raw-episode store is as good or better; agents given the choice keep raw episodes. Re-opened and confirmed in the source paper (Zhang 2026) across ARC-AGI Stream, ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, AppWorld; ACE independently shows one 18,282 to 122 token collapse from a full rewrite. No independent replication of Zhang itself; delta appends with dedup (ACE) and add plus delete without in-place edit (Zhang Table 5) avoid most of the harm.
agent_test: Compare raw cases vs consolidated lessons on a stream with distribution drift.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Curated memory beats append-everything for strong models: Dynamic Cheatsheet AIME 2024 Claude 3.5 Sonnet baseline 23.3, full-history 26.7, curated 50.0; GPT-4o full-history 6.7 vs baseline 20.0. Small models gain little or lose.
agent_test: Curated vs full-history at equal prompt tokens, across model strengths.

claim: Retention is not always beneficial: always retaining ground-truth cases hurt 4 of 12 tasks in CASCADE (retriever could not cope with larger bank); Memento's case memory hurt DeepResearcher in one ablation step; gains correlate with task similarity (r 0.717 / 0.563). Added: SEDM shows a relevant memory turned 73 failures into successes and 32 successes into failures; Sarukkai notes verified-success trajectories that fail when retrieved.
agent_test: Track per-task effect of memory; switch memory off when similarity to bank is low.

claim: Retrieving about 4 cases is enough; more adds nothing (Memento K=4 best, F1 64.5 / PM 78.5; CASCADE with 4 cases beats REINFORCE+LoRA on all 12 tasks).
agent_test: Sweep K=1,2,4,8 at equal tokens.

claim: A case bank with success-only retention can match or beat gradient fine-tuning on the tasks tested (CASCADE 66.68 vs REINFORCE+LoRA 58.93 on Qwen3-32B average; 9 of 12 tasks).
agent_test: Not testable for us (no training); use as justification only.

claim: Gains from memory continue to grow slowly over repeated passes and no inflexion was found (Memento no-CBR 78.65 to 84.47 vs parametric CBR 80.46 to 85.44; CBR gain +0.38 to +0.97 at pass 5).
agent_test: Long-stream run (more than 500 tasks) to look for saturation or decay.

claim: Explicit per-fact write operators (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP) and pre-write dedup / invalid filtering are cheap retention controls: Mem0 LOCOMO J 66.88, 91% lower latency than full context; AWM dedup plus invalid-action filter.
agent_test: Add a write-op step and compare size and accuracy.

claim: A code-checked verification gate before write (Voyager self-verification) is the most important feedback type: removing it cuts discovered items by 73%.
agent_test: Gate writes on executable checks where tasks allow it.

claim: Judge noise matters less for strategy-level memory (ReasoningBank similar success at simulated judge accuracy 70-90%), which conflicts with Xiong where coarse judges lost to strict ones. Update: counting Xiong Table 1, 6 of 12 coarse-judge cells beat the fixed seed bank and 6 do not; ReasoningBank judge was 72.7 percent accurate and even simulated 50 percent kept gains over no memory. Consistent with a store-format explanation but still untested head-to-head.
agent_test: Vary judge accuracy on our write gate and measure.

claim: Deleting by later-use utility is the only deletion rule shown to work with ordinary embedding retrieval; no study tests footprint or competence deletion with embeddings.
agent_test: Compare delete-by-later-use utility vs random vs age at a fixed cap on our stream.

claim: The CASCADE 20.9 percent headline is undefined in the text; on the 12-task Qwen3-32B table the gain is +18.35 points (38 percent relative) with a per-task range of +2.1 to +51.2 and a median of +15.7; 4 of 12 tasks gain under 6 points.
agent_test: Quote the 18.35 points and the spread, not 20.9.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Retention gain comes mainly from retrieving a task-relevant case, not from having any extra examples: ExpeL ALFWorld ReAct 40.0, random successful trajectories 42.5, task-similarity retrieval 59.0. Strong backbones gain little from replay (Qwen2.5-32B 0.82 with no replay, no clear gain).
agent_test: Add a random same-task-examples control at equal count to any memory test.

claim: Distilled or appended lesson stores tolerate write-gate noise much better than raw trace stores, and rewriting a store in place is the main source of decay.
agent_test: Same noisy gate on raw traces vs one-line lessons; measure final success.

claim: A cheap check for a retained success that may hurt later is to replay the task with and without the candidate case (SEDM) or to track outcome of tasks where it was retrieved (Sarukkai Q); the first costs a re-run, the second is free but needs retrieval counts.
agent_test: Add a retrieval-outcome counter per case and prune cases with high retrieval count and low success.

claim: Failure lessons add small, inconsistent gains over success-only retention once the format can use them (ReMe +0.7 Avg@4 and 0 Pass@4; ReasoningBank +3.2 on Shopping) and raw failures can hurt (Evo-Memory ExpRAG Gemini ALFWorld 0.59 to 0.25). No study controls token cost.
agent_test: Success-only vs success plus one-line failure lessons at equal prompt tokens.

claim: No LLM-agent study tests a novelty-only write gate vs add-success at equal bank size, none tests all four write gates in one setup, and none tests a success-only bank over 1000+ tasks with distribution shift; the longest streams found are 400 steps (Zhang) and 800 training tasks (Sarukkai).
agent_test: Run a small stream (600 tasks) with 4 gates and a mid-stream task-type shift.
